portal_hypertension.title: Development and internal validation of VA-BLED for 1-year esophageal variceal bleeding risk in cirrhosis.
portal_hypertension.authors: Denk D, Schröder S, Friedrich-Rust M

portal_hypertension.abstract: Esophageal variceal bleeding is a life-threatening complication of cirrhosis, yet current risk stratification targets portal hypertension stage and endoscopic stigmata instead of short-term bleeding probability. We evaluated whether a simple score built from routinely available variables could stratify 1-year esophageal variceal bleeding risk. We developed and internally validated two multivariable logistic models in a retrospective outcome-balanced cohort of 108 patients with esophageal varices (54 variceal bleeding, 54 no bleeding). VA-BLED BASE incorporated Child-Pugh score, normalized alanine aminotransferase, and current alcohol use. VA-BLED HISTORY additionally incorporated previous bl...

portal_hypertension.abstract: To evaluate the technical feasibility, hemodynamic effects, and early clinical outcomes of the 6-10 mm GORE VIATORR TIPS Endoprosthesis with Controlled Expansion, which extends the prior 8 mm deployment floor to 6 mm. This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent de novo transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) creation with the 6-10 mm device between April and July 2026. Technical success was defined as portosystemic pressure gradient (PSPG) below 12 mmHg or ≥ 50% reduction from baseline.
